# Botany As a botanist, it is your job to grow enough food to stop the chef from seeking "alternative sources". Grow lots of wheat, and when you get tired of that, grow weed. Make weed smoothies and spike drinks with nettles. Just keep growing plants, and you'll do great!
## Starting your shift First identify the machines around you that you will be using. Coordinate with the Chef to see if they want anything specific to be grown, otherwise grow wheat and bananas and whatever else you feel like growing. You may also grow plants for Chemistry (Medbay), the Bartender, or to sell by Cargo.
# Tools There are many tools that can be used to keep your crops healthy and growing. The Hydroponics Tray is where you will spend most of your time as a botanist.
## Hydroponics Tray
It's a hydroponics tray, it grows plants with water. First fill the tray with water, then add seeds. Hydroponics tray lights indicate different things depending on color and position: - [color=red]Red Light, Left[/color]: Dead plant that needs re-planting. Use a spade to remove the plant. - [color=orange]Flashing Orange Light, Center[/color]: The environment is sub-optimal. Check what is affecting the plant by Shift Clicking on it. It is likely weeds but it could be undesirable pressure or lack of oxygen. If weeds, use a mini hoe or spray 1 time with weed spray. Be warned, however, that overuse of weed killers can lead to unhealthy plants, possibly killing them. - [color=#0336ff]Blue Light, Right[/color]: Needs water. Use bucket on the water tank and fill the tray. - [color=green]Green Light, Left[/color]: Ready for harvest. Left click to harvest. - [color=yellow]Yellow Light, Right[/color]: Needs nutrients. Use any fruit and put it into the soil or get EZ nutrients from chemistry.
The lifecycle of a hydroponics tray is the following: - [color=lightgreen]Empty[/color]: no water, seed or nutrients - [color=lightgreen]Hydrated[/color]: you've added water to it (e.g. from a bottle or bucket). - [color=lightgreen]Ready for planting[/color]: you've added water and nutrients to it (i.e. fertilizer). - [color=lightgreen]Planted[/color]: you've added a seed to it - [color=lightgreen]Ready for Harvest[/color]: you've waited for the plant to grow - [color=lightgreen]Sampled[/color]: you've taken a sample (seed) - [color=lightgreen]Harvested[/color]: you've picked ready plants. Some plants will then grow again. Others will die and need replanting. - [color=lightgreen]Unhealthy[/color]: You've sampled too many seeds or sprayed it with deadly chemicals. The plant isn't coping too well. It'll continue to grow. Health can be restored by fertilizers or you can cut your losses and extract a seed (plant clippers) and replant. - [color=lightgreen]Old / Wilted[/color]: the plant has matured and will soon die. It will still be harvestable and you can extract seeds but only for a short duration. Extract the seed and then pluck it out / chop it down. - [color=lightgreen]Dead[/color]: the plant has been harvested and ceased growing. It should be plucked out / chopped down. No seeds can be extracted.
## Seed Extractor
It extracts seeds. Insert crop, receive seeds.
# Plant Genetics Like all other forms of life known to the TSF's states, plants pass traits to offspring in their genes. By manipulating plant genetics, botanists can produce plant varieties with desirable mutations that increase plant health and yield.
## Traits The phenotype, or set of observable characteristics and traits of a plant, can be determined through careful observation and study. A few common traits include:
- [color=lightgreen]Bioluminescence[/color]: plants with this trait glow in the dark - [color=lightgreen]High yield[/color]: plants with this trait yield more fruit per harvest - [color=lightgreen]Less water[/color]: plants with this trait require less water than normal to grow - [color=lightgreen]Ligneous[/color]: plants with this trait require sharp tools to harvest - [color=lightgreen]Long life[/color]: plants with this trait live for more harvest cycles before dying - [color=lightgreen]Low light[/color]: plants with this trait need less light than normal to grow - [color=lightgreen]Pest resistance[/color]: plants with this trait are more resistant to pests - [color=lightgreen]Seedless[/color]: plants with this trait do not produce viable seeds - [color=lightgreen]Weed resistance[/color]: plants with this trait suppress weed growth
You can determine the phenotype of a plant simply by growing them and observing them! This is how Gregor Mendel, father of genetics, studied them in 1866.
## Mutations Plants treated with [color=cyan]unstable mutagen[/color] will experience random genetic mutations, which can alter their genes and result in changes to their traits. You can save the plants with mutations you want by harvesting their seeds.
The more unstable mutagen you use, the more mutations you will get. Since many genes are vital to a plant's survival, most mutations will cause a plant to die.
Rare mutations can make a plant [color=yellow]exude gas when it ripens[/color] (rarer gases are much less likely), [color=yellow]demand a specific atmosphere[/color], [color=red]emit radiation[/color], or even [color=red]grab nearby people[/color]. If vines seize you, use the Tear free action.
The [color=cyan]plant analyzer[/color] (or an AgroScan PDA cartridge) shows genes, mutations, reagents, and tray status. The window stays open in an inactive hand or pocket. [color=cyan]Print label[/color] stamps a short tag (potency, reagents, mutations) onto a scanned [color=yellow]seed packet[/color].
[color=cyan]Botanical analyzer glasses[/color] overlay a health bar plus status squares: [color=#4aa8ff]blue[/color] low water, [color=#7dce4a]green[/color] weeds, [color=#e8d050]yellow[/color] harvest, [color=#f0c040]gold[/color] radiation.
Link trays to a [color=cyan]hydroponics console[/color] with a network configurator. Filter the list by [color=yellow]harvest / low water / radiation / carnivorous[/color]. The [color=cyan]Journal[/color] tab stores a named line (name + genes), prints a seed packet, or writes a [color=cyan]cultivar disk[/color].
## Tray light Each tray has three modes: [color=lightgreen]ambient[/color], [color=yellow]day[/color], and [color=cyan]shade[/color]. Cycle with alt-click on the tray or from the console.
Normal crops are fine under station lighting. If a line "wants sun", switch the tray to [color=yellow]day[/color] or it will wilt. Shade-lovers want [color=cyan]shade[/color]. Light-hungry cultivars and [color=lightgreen]photozyme[/color] barely matter until the tray is on Day.
## Woody plants A [color=lightgreen]ligneous[/color] plant will not come off with bare hands — you need a knife or clippers. In return, harvest drops [color=cyan]cloth tinted to that cultivar[/color], not a grey rag: one or two sheets, more if potency is high. Textile will thank you.
High potency also drops [color=cyan]juice[/color] (a glass of the plant's reagents) and [color=cyan]dried produce[/color] in the same color. Aloe (dermaline) or antirad (hyronalin) lines at about 45+ potency drop [color=cyan]salve[/color] and [color=cyan]tea[/color] with no chemist required.
## What mutagen actually rolls Unstable mutagen spins several wheels at once. More mutagen in the tray means more hits. Gases are a separate lottery: oxygen and nitrogen almost always, [color=yellow]Frezon[/color] only if you are very lucky (or unlucky).
This is what you will see on the tray, not the internal names. Common stuff first, all-shift hunts at the bottom.
### Common - [color=#88cc88]Unviable[/color]: the bush dies on its own in a few cycles. Yank it, don't wait. - [color=#88cc88]New juice[/color]: produce gains an extra reagent. Unique phytochemicals still will not appear until the plant already has the matching mutation or climate (see the list below).
### Occasional - [color=#88cc88]Slippery[/color]: fruit is a banana peel. Harmless, funny for security. - [color=#88cc88]Ligneous[/color]: needs a sharp tool, drops cloth. - [color=#88cc88]Screaming[/color]: it yells when harvested. Embarrassing, not lethal. - [color=#88cc88]Light shift[/color]: the plant starts preferring brighter or darker trays. Without this, Day/Shade and photozyme barely do anything.
### Rare - [color=#88cc88]Exudes gas[/color]: a ripe plant dumps gas into the room. Usually boring; sometimes plasma, tritium, or Frezon — call atmos, don't be a hero. - [color=#88cc88]Breathes gas[/color]: the tray needs a specific gas or the plant sickens. You can tune a room to keep a line alive. - [color=#88cc88]CO₂ filter[/color]: eats carbon dioxide and only that. Park it in a stuffy cabin — a living scrubber with no surprises. - [color=#e85858]Carnivorous vines[/color]: they grab whoever stands too close. If you get caught, use Tear free. Keep interns away. This old type is still in the pool. - [color=#88cc88]Pest-eater[/color]: a different carnivorous kind — it eats weeds and bugs in the tray and leaves people alone. A useful bush, not a trap.
### Very rare - [color=#88cc88]Antirad fruit[/color]: hyronalin in the produce, the bush itself does not glow. A medkit from the garden. - [color=#e85858]Radioactive[/color]: the plant irradiates the tray. Standing next to it hurts, but you can distill radbloom extract. Hunt it on purpose.
### Extra niches - [color=#88cc88]Drought-tolerant[/color]: barely drinks. Fewer bucket trips. - [color=#88cc88]Nitrogen fixer[/color]: barely needs fertilizer. - [color=#88cc88]Shade-adapted[/color]: wants the tray on Shade. - [color=#88cc88]Sun-lover[/color]: wants Day. Pairs with photozyme. - [color=#88cc88]Perennial[/color]: grows back after harvest instead of dying. - [color=#88cc88]Pest ward[/color]: bugs almost never take hold. - [color=#88cc88]Thin air[/color]: tolerates low pressure. - [color=#88cc88]Oxygen bloom[/color]: exhales oxygen. A living vent for a cabin. - [color=#88cc88]Aloe[/color]: dermaline in the fruit — a salve from the garden. - [color=#88cc88]Bitter antidote[/color]: dylovene in the fruit.
A loaded swab also works on a [color=cyan]seed packet[/color]: poke the packet, the line grafts, no tray needed.
[color=cyan]Gene stabilizer[/color] from NutriMax locks a line. Mutagen will not scramble that plant afterwards; swab grafting still works.
Trays can be [color=cyan]renamed from the console[/color] (`wheat-rad-3`), otherwise the list is just HYD-xxxx. Cargo pays more for bred packets: potency, mutations, and rare juices.
## Unique phytochemicals These reagents only show up in produce when the plant already has matching mutations or growing conditions:
- [color=lightgreen]Phyto-aether[/color]: potency 50+ - [color=lightgreen]Lignin resin[/color]: ligneous plants - [color=lightgreen]Cryo-chlorophyll[/color]: very cold ideal temperature - [color=lightgreen]Photozyme[/color]: high light requirement - [color=lightgreen]Necrotoxin sap[/color]: kudzu mutation - [color=lightgreen]Radbloom extract[/color]: radioactive plants - [color=lightgreen]Vine ichor[/color]: carnivorous vines - [color=lightgreen]Atmophyte[/color]: plants that consume or exude gas
A sterile swab can be printed from the biogenerator.
## Cross-Pollination A [color=cyan]sterile swab[/color] is not a "scramble everything and lose the seeds" lottery.
- From a living plant the swab picks up [color=yellow]that line's pollen[/color] (examine the swab to see whose). - On an empty tray the pollen sprouts — a [color=lightgreen]new plant of the same line[/color]. - On another living plant it [color=lightgreen]grafts[/color]: the host keeps its species, while mutations, juices, and gases from the pollen move over. Crossing no longer makes the hybrid seedless by itself. - On a [color=cyan]seed packet[/color] the same graft applies: poke the packet, the line takes. No tray required.
Pollen stays on the swab until you collect a different line. You cannot swab a dead plant.
